summary: Hermann Kulke was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Freiburg and his Habilitation at Heidelberg University, where he served from 1967 to 1988 before holding a chair at Kiel University (1988–2003).

Hermann Lommel worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He earned his doctorate under Jacob Wackernagel at the University of Göttingen, where he was an associate professor (1917–1920) before serving as ordinary professor at Goethe University Frankfurt (1920–1950).

Hermann Mittelberger was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna and later served at Utrecht University (~1968–1972) and as ordinary professor of comparative Indo-European linguistics at the University of Graz (1971–2003).

Hermann Møller was a linguist who studied at several universities, including Leipzig under Georg Curtius, where he completed his PhD in 1874–1875. He later held Privatdozent positions at Kiel University (1878) and the University of Copenhagen (1883).

Hermann Oesterley worked in Indology and other fields. He earned his PhD at the University of Göttingen and held posts as Privatdozent at Kiel University (1858–1861), at Göttingen State and University Library (1862–1872), and as custos at Wrocław University Library (1873–1891).

Hermann Oldenberg specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctorate and Habilitation at Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber, subsequently serving as ordinarius at Kiel University (1889–1908) and professor at the University of Göttingen (from 1908).

Hermann Olshausen was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kiel University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Berlin (~1817–1821), as ordinary professor of theology at the University of Königsberg (1827–1834), and at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1834–1839).

Hermann Osthoff was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He completed a PhD at Bonn under Hermann Usener and a Habilitation at Leipzig, later serving as Privatdozent at Leipzig (1875) and ordinarius and director at Heidelberg University from 1877.

Hermann Paul specialized in linguistics, completing his PhD at the University of Leipzig. He held professorships at the University of Freiburg (1874, 1877) and served as professor of German philology at the University of Munich from 1893 to 1916.

Hermann Sauppe worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He earned his doctorate at Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann, later serving as Privatdozent at Zurich (1833), chief librarian at Zentralbibliothek Zürich (1837), gymnasium director in Weimar (1845), and professor at Göttingen (1855).

Hermann Schlagintweit was a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He earned a PhD from the University of Munich (~1845–1848) and held a teaching post at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1851.

Hermann Usener was a scholar of religious studies, linguistics, and other fields who studied at Heidelberg, Munich, Göttingen, and Bonn. He held academic posts at the University of Bern (~1861–1863), University of Greifswald (~1863–1866), and University of Bonn (~1866–1905).

Hermann Walter, an Indologist, studied at Neuchâtel, Edinburgh, Tübingen, and Munich, earning a PhD under Ernst Kuhn by 1893. He served at McGill University from 1900 to 1936 as a lecturer and professor of Modern and Germanic Languages.

Hermann Weller was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen and Humboldt University of Berlin. He served as a Privatdozent (1930) and later as an honorary professor (1938–1952) at the University of Tübingen.

Hermann Wilhelm Ebel was a linguist who earned his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp. After teaching at secondary schools, he succeeded Bopp in 1872 as professor of comparative philology at Humboldt University of Berlin.

Hertha Krick was an Indologist who studied under Gerhard Oberhammer at the University of Vienna, earning her PhD (~1964–1972). She subsequently served as an assistant at the University of Vienna from 1972 until 1979.

Hervey DeWitt Griswold was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Union College, Union Theological Seminary, and Cornell University. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Forman Christian College (1894–1914) and visiting lecturer at Columbia University (1923–1929).

Hew McLeod was an Indologist, religious studies scholar, and historian who studied at Nelson College, the University of Otago, and SOAS University of London. He served on the editorial board (Redaktionsråd) at the University of Otago from ~1971 to 1997.

Heymann Steinthal was a scholar of linguistics and philosophy who studied under August Boeckh at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held long-term posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1850–1899) and the Hochschule für die Wissenschaft des Judentums (~1872–1899).
Hideaki Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies (博士課程) at Taisho University, where he also held a post as a researcher (研究員), attested in 1995.
